links.outcome: Medical QA accuracy with vs without knowledge-graph-backed validation of LLM reasoner outputs
links.effect: With Haiku-4.5, KG validation gave +0.61 pp over no validator; QKG with context matching gave +1.40 pp over no validator and +0.79 pp over KG without context matching (all p<0.05). With Qwen-3.6-Plus, QKG gain over no validator was +5.96 pp.
links.quote: With Haiku-4.5 as both the Reasoner and the Validator, KG-backed validation significantly improves over a no-validator baseline ($+0.61$ pp), and QKG with context matching yields the largest gain, outperforming both KG validation without context matching ($+0.79$ pp) and the no-validator baseline ($+1.40$ pp; paired McNemar, all $p<0.05$).

unlisted_practices: Context-dependent triplet validity in a knowledge graph, with patient-group-specific constraints used to check applicability of evidence to the patient context

screen.practice: knowledge graph-based validation with context matching (retrieval grounding)
screen.reason: Evaluates a deployment safeguard/pipeline (a reasoner-validator setup using context-sensitive knowledge graph verification vs no validation / standard KG) on medical QA benchmarks.
